## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/
Coverage: reading

MOLECULAR DYNAMICS / THERMOSTATS

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Thermostats: temperature control and distributions [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/
Coverage: reading

Compare fluctuations, ergodicity and time correlations as well as mean temperature, from Nosé–Hoover and velocity rescaling to stochastic and momentum-conserving methods.
Two of the 12 methods have dedicated implementations: Langevin and CSVR. Preserve the earlier one-degree-of-freedom harmonic Langevin/BAOAB case. A separate edition compares both baths with the same OBABO splitting for a nondegenerate two-degree harmonic system and a two-degree anharmonic system with quartic coefficient lambda=0.2, and checks the standalone CSVR kinetic-energy kernel. The other 10 methods remain planned.
JSON · Markdown

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Define the controlled temperature [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#temperature
Coverage: reading

With kinetic energy K and f active degrees of freedom, the kinetic temperature is T = 2 K / (f k_B). Count constraints and removed center-of-mass motion consistently, and separate thermal motion from streaming. State whether rotational degrees of freedom are included.

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Equal mean temperature does not imply equal distributions [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#fluctuations
Coverage: reading

For f independent momentum degrees of freedom with classical quadratic kinetic energy, canonical equilibrium gives 2 K/(k_B T₀) a chi-square distribution with f degrees of freedom. Its mean K is f k_B T₀/2 and variance is f(k_B T₀)²/2. Direct rescaling v ← √(T₀/T) v fixes K immediately after application, removing these fluctuations. CSVR instead uses a stochastic factor to generate fluctuations.

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Separate sampling from dynamics [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#dynamics
Coverage: reading

An invariant distribution does not ensure adequate finite-time exploration. Even correct equilibrium sampling can coexist with friction- or collision-induced changes in velocity autocorrelations and diffusion. Assess integration error, heat-bath coupling time and random-seed dependence.

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — CSVR and Langevin: shared canonical targets, distinct correlations [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/
Coverage: reading

The new comparison is limited to small classical systems. CSVR and Langevin use matched OBABO splitting, degrees of freedom, temperature, potential and observation times. Distribution, fluctuations and correlations are separate diagnostics. The earlier BAOAB harmonic results remain in their original release.

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — The stochastic CSVR update and its sign [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#csvr-exact
Coverage: reading

CSVR evolves the total kinetic energy stochastically and scales all momenta together. The implementation uses the 2007 kinetic-energy SDE and exact propagator, with the signed factor in the 2008 paper. Here h denotes a thermostat substep.
The same Gaussian R determines energy and sign. Momentum flips matter for a few degrees of freedom. Draw S directly from a chi-square law with f−1 degrees, with S=0 at f=1; this avoids the Gamma-construction typo identified by the original author.
dK=\frac{\bar K-K}{\tau}\,dt+2\sqrt{\frac{K\bar K}{f\tau}}\,dWc=e^{-h/\tau},\quad a=\frac{(1-c)\bar K}{f},\quad K^+=\left(\sqrt{cK}+\sqrt a\,R\right)^2+aS,\quad R\sim N(0,1),\quad S\sim\chi^2_{f-1}\alpha=\operatorname{sign}\!\left(\sqrt{cK}+\sqrt a\,R\right)\sqrt{K^+/K},\qquad p_i^+=\alpha p_i
Sources: Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling · Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes · Algorithms: stochastic velocity rescaling, author correction note

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Compare with the same splitting [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#matched-splitting
Coverage: reading

Both new methods use O(Δt/2)–B(Δt/2)–A(Δt)–B(Δt/2)–O(Δt/2) for MD step Δt: A moves coordinates, B applies forces and O is the thermostat. The CSVR formula uses bath substep h=Δt/2. They share a velocity-Verlet core and differ in the bath updates.
Set τ=(2γ)⁻¹ to match kinetic-energy relaxation for the force-free bath. This τ is not the friction time γ⁻¹. At f=1, signed CSVR has the Langevin transition law; a paired-noise check tests the implementation.
The earlier BAOAB example uses a different B–A–O–A–B splitting. Its release and independent linear reference remain unchanged; the new OBABO references and errors do not replace them.
\tau=(2\gamma)^{-1},\qquad p^+=e^{-\gamma h}p+\sqrt{m k_B T_0(1-e^{-2\gamma h})}\,R_{\rm phys}\quad(f=1)
Sources: Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Three separate questions: distribution, fluctuation and correlation [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#distribution-fluctuation-correlation
Coverage: reading

Both methods share the static canonical target. Check momentum, kinetic energy and instantaneous-temperature distributions, means and variances. Position references are analytic for harmonic systems and use separate quadrature for the anharmonic case. Matching the mean temperature alone does not check fluctuations.
Dynamic correlations depend on the method and coupling time. Measure position q, momentum p, kinetic energy K and total energy H without requiring agreement between methods. For harmonic Langevin, distinguish the continuous matrix exponential from the OBABO discrete stationary covariance/propagator. Other full-system correlations are measured with uncertainty and timestep dependence.
The exact ρK(t)=exp(−t/τ) reference applies only to the isolated bath. Full harmonic or anharmonic motion exchanges K and U, so that expression is not used as its correlation target.
CDF errors are maxima over predeclared checkpoints: five position/energy points and, for the conditional bath, three quantile points. They are not Kolmogorov–Smirnov suprema over the whole distribution. Full-system correlations use canonical-reference centering and normalization, so finite-step zero-lag values need not equal one exactly.

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Three separate questions: distribution, fluctuation and correlation [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#distribution-fluctuation-correlation
Coverage: reading

K=\sum_{i=1}^{f}\frac{p_i^2}{2m_i},\quad \bar K=\frac{f k_B T_0}{2},\quad T_{\rm inst}=\frac{2K}{f k_B}\frac{2K}{k_B T_0}\sim\chi_f^2,\quad \operatorname{Var}K=\frac{f(k_B T_0)^2}{2},\quad \operatorname{Var}T_{\rm inst}=\frac{2T_0^2}{f}C_X(t)=\langle(X(t)-\langle X\rangle)(X(0)-\langle X\rangle)\rangle,\qquad \rho_X(t)=C_X(t)/C_X(0)\mathbb E[K^+\mid K]=cK+fa,\quad\operatorname{Var}(K^+\mid K)=2fa^2+4acK,\quad \rho_K(t)=e^{-t/\tau}\ \text{(bath only)}

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Sampling limits and implementation boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#sampling-and-boundaries
Coverage: reading

Preservation from a canonical initial ensemble and relaxation from temperature-perturbed starts are distinct checks. Use independent replicas, fixed seeds and finite observation windows; separate sampling uncertainty from timestep and coupling effects. These small tests do not guarantee mixing from arbitrary starts. Correlation standard errors use the spread of products across independent replicas at each lag; they are not uncertainties of a single-trajectory time average or an effective-sample-size estimate. No independent dynamical reference is claimed for the anharmonic full-system correlations, which are not presented as having zero error.
A common scaling factor does not directly randomize momentum direction. A correct K distribution cannot rule out restricted sampling from invariant conditions such as zero total momentum in a symmetric system, or from invariant subspaces. The adopted degrees of freedom include no added constraints or removed center-of-mass mode.
For a positive bath step, at K=0 the direction is undefined, so this implementation rejects global rescaling explicitly. It does not inject an arbitrary direction as an undocumented algorithm. Nonfinite or nonphysical parameters are also checked.
Sources: Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Primary sources for the adopted equations [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/
Coverage: reading

G. Bussi, D. Donadio and M. Parrinello (2007). Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling · DOI: 10.1063/1.2408420
Checked author-manuscript sections II.1–II.3, kinetic SDE (7), and appendix A (16)–(22); consult the author correction for Gamma-based squared-noise generation.
G. Bussi and M. Parrinello (2008). Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes · DOI: 10.1016/j.cpc.2008.01.006
Checked manuscript sections I–II, τ=(2γ)⁻¹, finite-step (8)–(9) and f=1; bibliography cross-checked with SISSA.
Giovanni Bussi (2026). Algorithms: stochastic velocity rescaling, author correction note
Checked the author note identifying the 2007 Gamma-generation typo. Year denotes access, not the correction publication year.

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Runnable CSVR/Langevin validations [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/
Coverage: reading

Compare bath choices under the same OBABO splitting; separate step/coupling effects and independent-stream sampling uncertainty. Check distributions and temperature fluctuations separately from correlations. Langevin and CSVR correlations need not agree: they describe method-dependent sampling dynamics.
Langevin thermostat: canonical distributions, timestep bias and correlation · ZIP · Stored results · Rerun receipt
Distribution checks use a harmonic potential and fixed seeds. Exact position variance does not remove finite-step momentum bias. Evidence does not transfer to other thermostats, general molecules or long ab initio MD.
Exact CSVR bath: conditional laws, fluctuations and kinetic correlation · ZIP · Stored results · Rerun receipt
A bath diagnostic, not another independent physical problem. Correct K sampling does not thermalize momentum directions by global scaling alone. The bath-only exp(−t/tau) identity is not a full-MD kinetic ACF. Statistical decisions apply to fixed seeds/budgets, not general mixing guarantees.
CSVR versus Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations of two harmonic modes · ZIP · Stored results · Rerun receipt

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Runnable CSVR/Langevin validations [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/
Coverage: reading

Global-CSVR and local-Langevin dynamical correlations are not required to agree. CDF errors are maxima over five declared points, not whole-line KS distances. Canonical-start preservation and the heated-start finite-time check do not prove ergodicity; tests retain an invariant unexcited-axis counterexample. No extrapolation to molecules, constraints or BOMD.
Anharmonic CSVR versus Langevin: distribution checks against Boltzmann quadrature · ZIP · Stored results · Rerun receipt
A small example for one separable two-mode quartic potential and fixed seeds. H is not treated as harmonic Gamma. No independent exact full-system dynamical reference is claimed, and neither matching correlations nor time order hidden by sampling noise is an acceptance claim. Molecular transport, quantum and ab initio MD are outside scope.

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Direct velocity rescaling [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#velocity-rescaling
Coverage: reading

Multiply velocities by a common factor to set the kinetic energy at each application. Simple deterministic rescaling does not reproduce canonical kinetic-energy fluctuations.
A comparison case for distinguishing temperature control from canonical sampling. Ratio-based rescaling is undefined at T=0; the application interval also matters.
Other names: ベロシティースケーリング / ベロシティスケーリング / velocity scaling / simple velocity rescaling
Method status, JSON and Markdown
GROMACS: temperature coupling

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Berendsen weak-coupling thermostat [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#berendsen-thermostat
Coverage: reading

Relax the temperature difference over a chosen coupling time using velocity scaling. Fluctuations are suppressed, so this is not a correct canonical sampler.
Treat as a historical relaxation method; do not assume correct NVT fluctuations or response properties.
Other names: ベルンゼン / Berendsen thermostat / weak coupling
Method status, JSON and Markdown
Berendsen et al. (1984), Molecular dynamics with coupling to an external bath
GROMACS: temperature coupling

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Andersen thermostat [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#andersen-thermostat
Coverage: reading

Represent stochastic heat-bath collisions by redrawing selected particle velocities from a Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution.
Canonical sampling and physical time correlations are separate criteria. Independent velocity redraws alter total momentum and transport.
Other names: アンダーセン / stochastic collisions
Method status, JSON and Markdown
Andersen (1980), Molecular dynamics simulations at constant pressure and/or temperature
GROMACS: temperature coupling

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Langevin thermostat [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#langevin-thermostat
Coverage: reading

Langevin thermostat: canonical distributions, timestep bias and correlation: Compare harmonic BAOAB with canonical and discrete-Lyapunov stationary distributions, and with continuous/discrete time correlations. CSVR versus Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations of two harmonic modes: Compare global CSVR with local Langevin on two nondegenerate modes using the same OBABO splitting. Record position, momentum, temperature and total-energy distributions, fluctuations and correlations. Anharmonic CSVR versus Langevin: distribution checks against Boltzmann quadrature: Compare CSVR and Langevin distributions, temperature/energy fluctuations and correlations for two weakly quartic modes. Independent Boltzmann quadrature provides equilibrium references.
Friction changes dynamical correlations and diffusion. Finite-step sampling errors must be assessed together with the integration scheme.
Other names: ランジュバン / ランジュヴァン / friction and noise
Method status, JSON and Markdown
Bussi & Parrinello (2007), Accurate sampling using Langevin dynamics
LAMMPS: fix langevin

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Nosé extended-system thermostat [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#nose-thermostat
Coverage: reading

Introduce additional heat-bath degrees of freedom and time scaling: a starting point for deterministic constant-temperature molecular dynamics.
Distinguish the original extended Hamiltonian from the real-time Nosé–Hoover equations. An invariant distribution alone does not establish ergodicity.
Other names: ノセ / 能勢 / Nose thermostat / extended system
Method status, JSON and Markdown
Nosé (1984), A unified formulation of the constant temperature molecular dynamics methods

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Nosé–Hoover thermostat [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#nose-hoover
Coverage: reading

A deterministic method with a dynamically adjusted heat-bath friction variable. The canonical distribution is invariant, but small systems can fail to explore it ergodically.
Check nonergodicity in systems such as harmonic oscillators and dependence on bath mass or coupling time. Mean temperature is insufficient validation.
Other names: のせフーバー / ノセフーバー / ノセ・フーバー / 能勢・フーバー / Nose-Hoover
Method status, JSON and Markdown
Hoover (1985), Canonical dynamics: Equilibrium phase-space distributions
GROMACS: temperature coupling

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Nosé–Hoover chains [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#nose-hoover-chains
Coverage: reading

Couple heat-bath variables to further heat baths in a chain. This extension addresses sampling problems of a single thermostat.
Chain length, masses and substeps matter. Adding a chain does not universally guarantee ergodicity.
Other names: ノセ・フーバー鎖 / NHC / Nose-Hoover chain
Method status, JSON and Markdown
Martyna, Klein & Tuckerman (1992), Nosé–Hoover chains: The canonical ensemble via continuous dynamics

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Gaussian isokinetic thermostat [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#gaussian-isokinetic
Coverage: reading

Constrain kinetic energy continuously using a constraint force, connecting nonequilibrium molecular dynamics with constrained mechanics.
Distinguish fixed kinetic energy from the fluctuating canonical kinetic energy at finite system size. Configurational and full phase-space distributions differ.
Other names: ガウス等運動エネルギー / isokinetic constraint

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Generalized Langevin equation (GLE) [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#generalized-langevin
Coverage: reading

Use memory kernels and colored noise, or auxiliary variables representing them, to tailor the frequency response of a heat bath.
Separate classical equilibrium fluctuation–dissipation settings from nonequilibrium approximations to nuclear quantum effects; neither is an electronic-structure solver.

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — DPD pair thermostat [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#dpd-thermostat
Coverage: reading

Control temperature using dissipative and random pair forces. Standard symmetric pair forces conserve the pair’s total momentum.
Relevant when momentum transport matters. Verify matched friction/noise, radial weights and finite-step effects.
Other names: 散逸粒子動力学 / dissipative particle dynamics / pairwise thermostat

## Thermostats: temperature control and distributions — Lowe–Andersen thermostat [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/thermostats/#lowe-andersen
Coverage: reading

Stochastically redraw a component of a nearby pair’s relative velocity while preserving the pair’s center-of-mass momentum.
Distinguish from independent-particle Andersen collisions. Collision frequency and neighbor radius affect transport such as viscosity and diffusion.
Other names: ロウ・アンダーセン / Lowe Andersen
Method status, JSON and Markdown
Lowe (1999), An alternative approach to dissipative particle dynamics

## Time integration and leapfrog — Time integration and leapfrog [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/time-integration/
Coverage: reading

Spatial reconstruction and time integration are independent choices. After spatial discretization, a PDE becomes an ODE system dU/dt = L(U). Accuracy, stability, monotonicity, dissipation, and cost then depend on both parts. The time integration notebook isolates the temporal choice using y′ = i y, y(0) = 1.

## Time integration and leapfrog — Twelve methods on one oscillator# [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/time-integration/#twelve-methods-on-one-oscillator
Coverage: reading

The exact solution exp(i t) follows the unit circle. Forward Euler and backward Euler are first order: the former grows on this undamped oscillator, while the latter damps it. The explicit RK2 family includes Heun / SSPRK(2,2), explicit midpoint, and Ralston. Kutta RK3, SSPRK(3,3), and SSPRK(4,3) are third order; classical RK4 and SSPRK(5,4) are fourth order. Implicit midpoint is second order and preserves the amplitude of this linear oscillator. Its phase still has error. Read the RK family chapter and use the family notebook for stage/order/SSP comparisons and nonlinear tests.
For y′ = lambda y, define z = lambda delta t. One-step amplification factors include
R_{\rm FE}=1+z,\quad R_{\rm BE}=\frac1{1-z},\quad
R_{\rm midpoint}=\frac{1+z/2}{1-z/2}.
The RK factors are the exponential Taylor polynomial through degree two, three, or four for the three RK2 variants, Kutta RK3 / SSPRK(3,3), or classical RK4 on this scalar linear equation. SSPRK(4,3) instead has a degree-four term z⁴/48; SSPRK(5,4) has an additional degree-five term. Shared scalar amplification does not make nonlinear RK stages identical. SSP properties depend on a forward-Euler bound for the spatial operator; they are not unconditional stability.

## Time integration and leapfrog — Leapfrog needs two roots# [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/time-integration/#leapfrog-needs-two-roots
Coverage: reading

The centered, two-step first-order-system recurrence is
y^{n+1}=y^{n-1}+2z y^n,\qquad
\xi_\pm=z\pm\sqrt{1+z^2}.
The root tending to +1 as z tends to zero carries the physical mode; the root tending to −1 carries a computational mode alternating between steps. Both roots and their multiplicities matter. For z = i sigma, distinct roots have unit modulus when |sigma| < 1. At |sigma| = 1 the repeated root can give linearly growing solutions; do not include that endpoint in a general boundedness claim. Above it, one root grows geometrically.
A starting value is required in addition to y(0). This implementation takes one RK4 step, optionally adding a real perturbation epsilon to y(1). At lambda = 0 that perturbation gives even samples equal to 1 and odd samples equal to 1+epsilon: a direct computational-mode demonstration. For the notebook’s oscillator it also perturbs the physical mode.
Time filters such as the Robert–Asselin family modify this behavior, with their own damping and accuracy tradeoffs; see Williams (2009). No filter is applied in this edition.

## Time integration and leapfrog — Particle leapfrog is a different formulation# [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/time-integration/#particle-leapfrog-is-a-different-formulation
Coverage: reading

A staggered kick–drift scheme for position and velocity, or velocity Verlet for a second-order mechanical system, is often also called leapfrog. Its variables live at different temporal locations and its symplectic interpretation uses that structure. The scalar recurrence above is not a demonstration of a complete SPH particle integrator or a proof of long-time energy conservation for general mechanics.

## Time integration and leapfrog — Reproduce and read the notebook# [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/time-integration/#reproduce-and-read-the-notebook
Coverage: reading

from numart.time_integration import linear_trajectory, leapfrog_roots
t, y = linear_trajectory(rate=1j, dt=0.1, steps=200, method='leapfrog')
print(leapfrog_roots(0.1j))
The browser selects from Python-computed trajectories with fixed final time 20, twelve methods, seven step sizes, and three leapfrog starting perturbations. Axes expand for unstable samples. A matching time interval is not an equal-cost comparison: implicit solves and RK stages differ. Tests measure temporal refinement orders and check the leapfrog roots, alternating mode, and midpoint amplitude. These oscillator trajectories evaluate the scalar stability factor, which is algebraically equivalent to RK stages on this linear test equation; the separate family notebook evaluates full nonlinear stages.
Continue with the spatial stability laboratory, SPH, and ALE.

## Time integration and leapfrog — Canonical mechanical maps# [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/time-integration/#canonical-mechanical-maps
Coverage: reading

The symplectic integration chapter now implements mechanical kick–drift–kick Verlet, a fourth-order Yoshida composition, symplectic Euler, and implicit midpoint on harmonic and quartic Hamiltonians. The map notebook compares them with RK4, separating canonical structure from exact energy conservation.

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-nonlinear-assumptions
Coverage: reading

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-nonlinear-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Strang-compose exact half-step diffusion of the FD matrix, diagonalized by FFT with symbol −4sin²(πk/N)/dx², and a full implicit-midpoint reaction step solved by local2×2 Newton iterations. FFT does not change FD space into spectral space. Fail on nonconvergence/budget excess; never clip concentrations.
u_t=D_u u_{xx}+a-u+u^2v,\qquad v_t=D_v v_{xx}+b-u^2v\frac{d\langle u+v\rangle}{dt}=a+b-\langle u\rangle,\quad S_{n+1}-S_n=h(a+b-\langle\bar u\rangle)\lambda_{h,k}=-4\sin^2(\pi k/N)/\Delta x^2,\quad\Phi_h=e^{hDL_h/2}\,\Phi_{\rm midpoint}^{F}(h)\,e^{hDL_h/2}\|e\|_1=\max_s\frac1N\sum_j|e_{s,j}|,\quad\|e\|_2=\max_s\sqrt{\frac1N\sum_j e_{s,j}^2},\quad\|e\|_\infty=\max_{s,j}|e_{s,j}|

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-nonlinear-validation
Coverage: reading

Compare raw L1/L2/L∞ with a spatially independent cosine Fourier–Galerkin/Radau reference (K32/64/96, cubic projection M=4(K+1)>4K, analytic Jacobian). Separately check K and ODE-tolerance sensitivity. Measure time order against a separately implemented Radau integration of the SAME FD semidiscretization. Norms are per-species mean-absolute/RMS/maximum, then the worse species. Record source/sink balance, every-step positive concentrations, initially absent k≥5 (first allowed k6 here), and departure from linearization. Convergence norms and reference sensitivities are assessed at the fixed final time; intermediate snapshot errors are separate evolution diagnostics.

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-nonlinear-limits
Coverage: reading

A selected-symmetry1D educational model: no test of free noise-driven wavenumber selection, phase stability,2D spots or biological calibration. Not an original-paper reproduction. Implicit midpoint is A-stable but not L-stable or unconditionally positive; reactions do not conserve u+v. The initial coarse protocol failed; temporal resolution was strengthened while retaining every acceptance threshold and the failed record. No quantum calculations.

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-nonlinear-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
A. M. Turing (1952). The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis · DOI: 10.1098/rstb.1952.0012
Review scope / review_level: original-paper-selected-sections
Checked the university-hosted original scan, sections 6–7 (printed pp.46–50), ring formulation/linearization and bibliography. Distinct from the adopted coefficients, finite-amplitude reference and mature shape.
J. Schnakenberg (1979). Simple chemical reaction systems with limit cycle behaviour · DOI: 10.1016/0022-5193(79)90042-0
Review scope / review_level: official-bibliography-and-publisher-indexed-abstract
Checked official PubMed bibliography/DOI and publisher-indexed abstract. Full text returned403. Historical source for the reaction family, not a claim to reproduce original coefficients or experiments.
G. Strang (1968). On the Construction and Comparison of Difference Schemes · DOI: 10.1137/0705041
Review scope / review_level: original-paper-selected-nonlinear-composition
Checked original pp.510–512 for half-step composition and nonlinear second-order construction. This does not guarantee positivity or accuracy at arbitrary steps in the adopted model.
E. Hairer (2010). Geometric Numerical Integration, Lecture2

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-nonlinear-references
Coverage: reading

Review scope / review_level: author-lecture-selected-midpoint-and-splitting
Checked theorem3 and section5 of the author-hosted lecture for implicit-midpoint formula/order and symmetric splitting. Hamiltonian symplectic claims are not transferred to this chemical model.
The SciPy community (2024). SciPy1.14.1 solve_ivp and Radau reference
Review scope / review_level: official-versioned-api-specification
Checked official Radau IIA order5, local rtol/atol scaling, analytic Jacobians and termination status. ODE tolerances do not certify global continuum-PDE accuracy.

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-pattern-assumptions
Coverage: reading

1D periodic x∈[0,2π), a=.1,b=.9,D=(.01,1). Common IC u=1+.08cos(2x)+.01cos(4x), v=.9−.03cos(2x)−.002cos(4x), restricted to a reflection-even, pi-periodic invariant subspace with a fixed origin.

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-pattern-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Strang-compose exact half-step diffusion of the FD matrix, diagonalized by FFT with symbol −4sin²(πk/N)/dx², and a full implicit-midpoint reaction step solved by local2×2 Newton iterations. FFT does not change FD space into spectral space. Fail on nonconvergence/budget excess; never clip concentrations.
u_t=D_u u_{xx}+a-u+u^2v,\qquad v_t=D_v v_{xx}+b-u^2v\frac{d\langle u+v\rangle}{dt}=a+b-\langle u\rangle,\quad S_{n+1}-S_n=h(a+b-\langle\bar u\rangle)\lambda_{h,k}=-4\sin^2(\pi k/N)/\Delta x^2,\quad\Phi_h=e^{hDL_h/2}\,\Phi_{\rm midpoint}^{F}(h)\,e^{hDL_h/2}\|e\|_1=\max_s\frac1N\sum_j|e_{s,j}|,\quad\|e\|_2=\max_s\sqrt{\frac1N\sum_j e_{s,j}^2},\quad\|e\|_\infty=\max_{s,j}|e_{s,j}|

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-pattern-validation
Coverage: reading

Compare raw L1/L2/L∞ with a spatially independent cosine Fourier–Galerkin/Radau reference (K32/64/96, cubic projection M=4(K+1)>4K, analytic Jacobian). Separately check K and ODE-tolerance sensitivity. Measure time order against a separately implemented Radau integration of the SAME FD semidiscretization. Norms are per-species mean-absolute/RMS/maximum, then the worse species. Record source/sink balance, every-step positive concentrations, initially absent k≥5 (first allowed k6 here), and departure from linearization. Convergence norms and reference sensitivities are assessed at the fixed final time; intermediate snapshot errors are separate evolution diagnostics.

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-pattern-limits
Coverage: reading

A selected-symmetry1D educational model: no test of free noise-driven wavenumber selection, phase stability,2D spots or biological calibration. Not an original-paper reproduction. Implicit midpoint is A-stable but not L-stable or unconditionally positive; reactions do not conserve u+v. The initial coarse protocol failed; temporal resolution was strengthened while retaining every acceptance threshold and the failed record. No quantum calculations. Near-saturation refers to the reference90→100 test window; it proves no exact steady state, nonlinear stability or long-term attractor. A huge late linearized difference diagnoses failure of linearization, not numerical error.

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-pattern-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
A. M. Turing (1952). The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis · DOI: 10.1098/rstb.1952.0012
Review scope / review_level: original-paper-selected-sections
Checked the university-hosted original scan, sections 6–7 (printed pp.46–50), ring formulation/linearization and bibliography. Distinct from the adopted coefficients, finite-amplitude reference and mature shape.
J. Schnakenberg (1979). Simple chemical reaction systems with limit cycle behaviour · DOI: 10.1016/0022-5193(79)90042-0
Review scope / review_level: official-bibliography-and-publisher-indexed-abstract
Checked official PubMed bibliography/DOI and publisher-indexed abstract. Full text returned403. Historical source for the reaction family, not a claim to reproduce original coefficients or experiments.
G. Strang (1968). On the Construction and Comparison of Difference Schemes · DOI: 10.1137/0705041
Review scope / review_level: original-paper-selected-nonlinear-composition
Checked original pp.510–512 for half-step composition and nonlinear second-order construction. This does not guarantee positivity or accuracy at arbitrary steps in the adopted model.
E. Hairer (2010). Geometric Numerical Integration, Lecture2

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-pattern-references
Coverage: reading

Review scope / review_level: author-lecture-selected-midpoint-and-splitting
Checked theorem3 and section5 of the author-hosted lecture for implicit-midpoint formula/order and symmetric splitting. Hamiltonian symplectic claims are not transferred to this chemical model.
The SciPy community (2024). SciPy1.14.1 solve_ivp and Radau reference
Review scope / review_level: official-versioned-api-specification
Checked official Radau IIA order5, local rtol/atol scaling, analytic Jacobians and termination status. ODE tolerances do not certify global continuum-PDE accuracy.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Download and execute the supplement [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#run-all
Coverage: reading

Run inside atlas-foundations-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 4 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory.
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output
Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Matrix-based AMG: distinguish residual and solution error [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/
Coverage: reading

Build a smoothed-aggregation hierarchy from an SPD matrix alone and run V-cycles. Problems with 7², 15² and 31² unknowns distinguish independent sparse direct solutions, analytic discrete sine modes and second-order convergence to the continuum solution.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#sa-amg-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Dimensionless unit square, constant-positive-coefficient −Δu=f, homogeneous Dirichlet boundaries and five-point differences. Hierarchy setup receives no coordinates, mesh width or n; it uses the coefficient matrix and an implicit constant near-null candidate. A real SPD input is assumed; arbitrary indefinite problems are outside scope.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#sa-amg-algorithm
Coverage: reading

A graph based on row-relative off-diagonal strength supplies greedy star aggregates; leftover nodes attach to adjacent aggregates. Smooth tentative T via P=(I−ωD⁻¹A)T with ω=4/(3ρ̄), where ρ̄ bounds the absolute row sums of D⁻¹A. Coarse operators are PᵀAP. V-cycles use two pre/post Jacobi sweeps and a terminal dense direct solve. This is a small adopted SA variant, not every construction or convergence theorem in the original paper.
A_c=P^TAP,\quad P=(I-\omega D^{-1}A)Tr_k=b-Ax_k,\quad \eta_k=\|r_k\|_2/\|b\|_2

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#sa-amg-validation
Coverage: reading

Store normalized residuals, relative solution differences against SciPy spsolve, discrete-L²-type continuum errors, observed order and operator complexity. A randomly permuted matrix is also checked against a direct solution to expose hidden geometric ordering assumptions. A zero cycle budget reports nonconvergence.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#sa-amg-limits
Coverage: reading

Only three fixed scalar grids are checked. Large coefficient jumps, strong anisotropy, elasticity, arbitrary unstructured meshes, optimal complexity and mesh-independent convergence are not certified. A small residual alone does not prove a small solution error.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Householder QR and one-sided Jacobi SVD: orthogonality, rank and least squares [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/
Coverage: reading

Original Householder QR and one-sided Jacobi SVD for real tall matrices are checked on ordinary, 10⁶-column-scaled and rank-deficient inputs, against separate LAPACK singular values and minimum-norm least-squares solutions.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#qr-svd-factorization-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Small real matrices with m≥n. Numerical rank uses a 10⁻¹² threshold relative to the largest singular value; compact factors omit null directions. QR has no column pivoting and is not used as a rank-revealing method.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#qr-svd-factorization-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Householder reflectors triangularize R while accumulating Q. The SVD repeatedly rotates column pairs toward orthogonality and uses their resulting lengths as singular values; it does not diagonalize AᵀA. Least squares uses triangular back substitution for QR and truncated compact SVD for deficient rank.
A=QR,\quad Q^TQ=IA\simeq U_r\Sigma_rV_r^T,\quad x_{\min}=V_r\Sigma_r^{-1}U_r^Tb

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#qr-svd-factorization-validation
Coverage: reading

Compare QR/SVD relative reconstruction, Q/U/V orthogonality, singular values from SciPy LAPACK gesdd, least-squares solutions/ranks from gelsd/gelsy and normal-equation stationarity residuals. Singular-vector signs are not compared; zero matrices and budget exhaustion are tested.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#qr-svd-factorization-limits
Coverage: reading

Not a full LAPACK replacement or validation of complex/wide matrices, arbitrary extreme scales or optimal relative singular-value accuracy. The 10⁻¹² cutoff defines numerical rather than exact mathematical rank. The experiment does not establish all hypotheses of the Demmel–Veselić accuracy results.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Lanczos and Arnoldi: convergence of Ritz values and eigenpair residuals [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/
Coverage: reading

Original Lanczos and Arnoldi on symmetric/nonsymmetric 32×32 and 48×48 matrices measure convergence of the largest-real-part eigenpair over Krylov dimensions 4, 8 and 16, against independent full-matrix LAPACK references.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#krylov-eigenvalues-assumptions
Coverage: reading

The symmetric case is real symmetric; the nonsymmetric case is real with a known separated largest eigenvalue 5. Starting vectors use fixed seeds. Nonsymmetric Ritz values may be complex and are selected by largest real part.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#krylov-eigenvalues-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Lanczos uses its three-term recurrence plus two passes of full reorthogonalization; Arnoldi uses two-pass modified Gram–Schmidt. Only the small projected T/H is solved by NumPy eigh/eig before lifting Ritz vectors. A full dense solve of the original matrix is used only on the reference side.
AV_m=V_mH_m+h_{m+1,m}v_{m+1}e_m^TH_my=\theta y,\quad v=V_my,\quad r=Av-\theta v

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#krylov-eigenvalues-validation
Coverage: reading

Store ||Av−λv||₂, differences from independently solved dense eigenvalues and basis orthogonality; verify final improvement as Krylov dimension grows. Nonsymmetric Ritz convergence is not assumed monotone. Tests include identity-matrix happy breakdown, zero-start rejection and insufficient dimension budgets.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#krylov-eigenvalues-limits
Coverage: reading

Unrestarted small-matrix educational examples with separated extreme eigenpairs. Interior/clustered eigenvalues, very large sparse matrices, strong nonnormality, shift-invert and implicitly restarted Arnoldi are outside scope. A small eigenpair residual alone is not treated as a rigorous eigenvalue-error bound for nonnormal matrices.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Gauss–Legendre and adaptive quadrature: exactness, error estimates and budgets [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/
Coverage: reading

Construct Gaussian nodes/weights from the Legendre recurrence and test polynomial moments through degree 2n−1 and an exponential. Adaptive Simpson integrates exponential and Lorentzian peaks, against analytic integrals and independent QUADPACK.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#gauss-adaptive-quadrature-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Dimensionless smooth real functions on finite intervals. Fixed Gauss orders 2/4/8/16 and adaptive absolute tolerances 10⁻⁵/10⁻⁷/10⁻⁹ are swept separately. Endpoint singularities, discontinuities and infinite intervals are not covered by these inputs.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#gauss-adaptive-quadrature-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Golub–Welsch obtains nodes from a symmetric Jacobi matrix and weights from twice the squared first eigenvector components. Adaptive Simpson bisects intervals and allocates tolerances using |Sleft+Sright−Swhole|/15 as a local estimate. Evaluation and depth limits report unmet targets explicitly.
\int_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,dx\simeq\sum_{j=1}^{n}w_jf(x_j)E_{\mathrm{est}}=|S_{\mathrm{left}}+S_{\mathrm{right}}-S_{\mathrm{whole}}|/15

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#gauss-adaptive-quadrature-validation
Coverage: reading

Measure polynomial moments for every chosen order, node/weight differences from SciPy roots_legendre, order refinement for the analytic exponential integral, and agreement with analytic arctangent and SciPy quad references. Store evaluation counts/errors as tolerance tightens; test forced exhaustion after five evaluations and nonfinite integrands.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#gauss-adaptive-quadrature-limits
Coverage: reading

The local Simpson estimate is not a rigorous error bound for arbitrary functions. The implementation does not generally solve missed high frequencies, singularities or roundoff stagnation, and it is not a reimplementation of Gauss–Kronrod or all of QUADPACK.

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd/#ct-glm-independent-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Reuse the published first-order Rusanov/forward-Euler solvers: shared corner-EMF discrete curl for CT and cell-centered hyperbolic/parabolic GLM cleaning. Independent Athena++ uses HLLD, PLM and RK2.
\nabla\cdot\mathbf B=0,\qquad \mathbf B_t+\nabla\times\mathbf E=0

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#gaussian-mcmc-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Use a log-acceptance Metropolis update. Pool FFT within-chain autocovariances and obtain mean-observable ESS from Geyer initial-positive pairs starting at gamma0+gamma1. Also report classical split-Rhat.

Coverage: reading

Use the normal CDF as an independent analytic reference and compare chain-mean RMSE at 1024/2048/8192 retained samples. A separate stationary AR(1) sequence and exact tau=(1+rho)/(1-rho) check the diagnostic. Acceptance is predeclared in fixed inputs.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#gaussian-mcmc-limits
Coverage: reading

Statistical checks apply to fixed seeds and budgets. ESS concerns the mean only; Rhat is not rank-normalized. No guarantee covers multimodality, high dimensions, every seed, mixing or a specified false-positive rate.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Langevin thermostat: canonical distributions, timestep bias and correlation [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/
Coverage: reading

Compare harmonic BAOAB with canonical and discrete-Lyapunov stationary distributions, and with continuous/discrete time correlations.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#langevin-harmonic-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Mass, Boltzmann constant, frequency, friction and temperature are one. Use 32768 replicas, burn time 20, steps 0.4/0.2/0.1 and correlation lag 2; require h*omega<2.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#langevin-harmonic-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Compose force B and drift A half steps with exact OU noise O in B-A-O-A-B order. Record covariance, three CDFs, energy mean/variance and position correlation.
dq=p\,dt,\qquad dp=-\omega^2q\,dt-\gamma p\,dt+\sqrt{2\gamma T}\,dW\Sigma=M\Sigma M^T+Q,\qquad \Sigma_{h}=\operatorname{diag}(T/\omega^2,T(1-h^2\omega^2/4))

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#langevin-harmonic-validation
Coverage: reading

Check against a SciPy discrete-Lyapunov solve and explicit harmonic covariance diag(T/omega²,T(1-h²omega²/4)). Separate second-order momentum bias from sampling error and evaluate burn transients from the map. A separate matrix exponential gives continuous correlation.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#langevin-harmonic-limits
Coverage: reading

Distribution checks use a harmonic potential and fixed seeds. Exact position variance does not remove finite-step momentum bias. Evidence does not transfer to other thermostats, general molecules or long ab initio MD.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Reaction-diffusion: separate second-order space and fourth-order time [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/
Coverage: reading

Validate a small linear diffusion-reaction operator against continuous and semidiscrete Fourier solutions.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#reaction-diffusion-fourier-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Periodic[0,2pi), D=0.1,r=0.1, initial cos(2x), final t=2. Use grids 16/32/64 and a separate fixed-grid timestep sequence 0.5/0.25/0.125.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#reaction-diffusion-fourier-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Advance original periodic second-centered differences with RK4. The spatial sequence uses one small time step; the temporal sequence fixes the spatial operator.
u_t=D u_{xx}+r u,\qquad u(x,t)=e^{(r-Dk^2)t}\cos(kx)\lambda_h=r-\frac{4D}{\Delta x^2}\sin^2(k\Delta x/2)

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#reaction-diffusion-fourier-validation
Coverage: reading

Measure spatial order against r-Dk² and temporal order against r-4Dsin²(kdx/2)/dx². Both are independent analytic references, rather than a finer-grid run of the same solver.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#reaction-diffusion-fourier-limits
Coverage: reading

Only a linear, periodic, smooth single mode is verified. Nonlinear Fisher fronts, complex boundaries, spatial ecosystems and general reaction networks remain outside scope.

Coverage: reading

Use a matrix exponential to validate stable homogeneous kinetics and diffusion-driven growth of a selected Schnakenberg mode.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#turing-schnakenberg-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Dimensionless a=0.1,b=0.9, equilibrium(1,0.9), diffusivities(0.01,1), periodic k=2 and initial amplitude1e-4. Restrict runs to linear t=1 and nonlinear t=4.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#turing-schnakenberg-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Advance the linearized and short nonlinear PDEs using original centered differences/RK4. Record mode amplitudes/growth on three grids, minimum concentrations and early-pattern amplification.
u_t=D_u u_{xx}+a-u+u^2v,\quad v_t=D_v v_{xx}+b-u^2v\partial_t\widehat{\delta z}=(J-k^2D)\widehat{\delta z},\quad \widehat{\delta z}(t)=e^{(J-k^2D)t}\widehat{\delta z}(0)

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#turing-schnakenberg-validation
Coverage: reading

Compare linear numerical fields with SciPy expm of continuum J-k²D and measure spatial convergence. Quantify the nonlinear run against a semidiscrete linear matrix exponential as a small-amplitude check, not validation of mature morphology.

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#turing-schnakenberg-limits
Coverage: reading

One near-equilibrium onset experiment. No claim reproduces original-paper parameters/experiments, mature patterns, wavenumber selection from random noise or biological calibration.

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#fitzhugh-nagumo-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Dimensionless a=0.7,b=0.8,tau=12.5. Start at resting equilibrium for I=0, apply I=0.8 only during t=10..20 and integrate to t=80. No calibration to physiological physical units.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#fitzhugh-nagumo-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Use original RK4 with steps 0.1/0.05/0.025, splitting time intervals exactly at pulse discontinuities. At output spacing 0.1, measure the peak and distance from rest.
\dot v=v-v^3/3-w+I(t),\qquad \dot w=(v+a-bw)/\tau

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#fitzhugh-nagumo-validation
Coverage: reading

Compare separate SciPy DOP853 at rtol=1e-11 and 1e-13 to check reference sensitivity; measure maximum solution error and time order against the tighter reference. Peak time is resolved only on the output grid.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#fitzhugh-nagumo-limits
Coverage: reading

Scoped verification of an FHN/BVP-style reduced ODE. It excludes full HH ion channels, spatial axons, patient data and experimental electrophysiology reproduction.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#fitzhugh-nagumo-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
R. FitzHugh (1961). Impulses and Physiological States in Theoretical Models of Nerve Membrane · DOI: 10.1016/S0006-3495(61)86902-6
Review scope / review_level: official-abstract-and-metadata
Original-paper abstract and bibliography in PubMed checked. Supports the two-variable excitable/refractory reduction; no full HH or measured membrane-voltage reproduction is claimed.
J. Nagumo, S. Arimoto and S. Yoshizawa (1962). An Active Pulse Transmission Line Simulating Nerve Axon · DOI: 10.1109/JRPROC.1962.288235
Review scope / review_level: publisher-abstract-and-metadata
IEEE publisher abstract, volume, pages and DOI checked. Historical source for reduced excitation and its circuit analogue; no spatial transmission-line or hardware-experiment reproduction is claimed.
The SciPy community (2024). SciPy1.14.1 solve_ivp reference
Review scope / review_level: official-api-documentation
Official DOP853, dense output, tolerance and success specifications checked. Implementation documentation for the separate numerical reference.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Download and execute the supplement [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#run-all
Coverage: reading

Run inside atlas-particles-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 6 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory.
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output
Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Neutral-cell Ewald sums and an independent theta integral [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/
Coverage: reading

Implement real-space, reciprocal-space and self Ewald terms for neutral 3D periodic Coulomb charges; vary splitting and cutoffs.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#ewald-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Cubic cell, zero total charge, Coulomb constant one and conducting/tin-foil boundary. An asymmetric eight-charge case is distinct from the eight-ion NaCl reference cell.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#ewald-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Combine an erfc-screened image sum, Gaussian-damped reciprocal structure factors and the self correction. Differentiate each term and check all 24 force components against central energy differences.
E=\frac12\sum_{ij\mathbf n}^{\prime}q_iq_j\frac{\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha r_{ij\mathbf n})}{r_{ij\mathbf n}}+\frac{2\pi}{V}\sum_{\mathbf k\ne0}\frac{e^{-k^2/(4\alpha^2)}}{k^2}|S(\mathbf k)|^2-\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt\pi}\sum_iq_i^2M_{\rm NaCl}=\frac2{\sqrt\pi}\int_0^\infty[1-\vartheta_4(0,e^{-u^2})^3]du

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#ewald-validation
Coverage: reading

Three splitting parameters, three real cutoffs and four reciprocal cutoffs. Check the NaCl Madelung constant against a separately implemented 1D Jacobi-theta integral, storing its quadrature error estimate.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#ewald-limits
Coverage: reading

No charged-cell/background correction, triclinic cell, finite-dielectric surface term, slab correction, stress or material-specific force field.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Mesh/order convergence of B-spline smooth PME [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/
Coverage: reading

A small smooth-PME example assigns charge with B-splines and evaluates the Ewald reciprocal contribution by FFT.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#spme-assumptions
Coverage: reading

The neutral cubic cell and real-space term match the Ewald example. The adopted PME-family variant uses Essmann-type B-splines, distinct from Darden’s original Lagrange interpolation.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#spme-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Tensor-product cardinal splines of order four or six spread the charges. Apply the nodal-spline discrete structure-factor correction and Gaussian Green function through 3D FFTs; analytically differentiate assignment weights for forces.
Q_{\mathbf j}=\sum_iq_i\prod_{a=1}^3M_p(u_{ia}-j_a+p/2)\mathbf F_i=-\partial E_h/\partial\mathbf r_i

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#spme-validation
Coverage: reading

Meshes 16³/24³/40³ and two orders are compared with directly summed Ewald reciprocal terms. Shared real/self terms are stated. Check finest-grid force derivatives by energy differences and verify assigned total charge.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#spme-limits
Coverage: reading

Finite-mesh aliasing permits nonzero net force for this energy-gradient variant; that diagnostic is reported. No exact momentum conservation, long MD, original PME, optimized P³M or slab validation is claimed.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — 2D logarithmic FMM with M2M, M2L and L2L [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/
Coverage: reading

Evaluate a free-space log potential with uniform-quadtree multipole and local expansions and compare with direct sums.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#fmm-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Particles lie in a unit-square bounding box, not a physical wall boundary. The kernel is phi=−sum(q log r), with field −grad(phi); self terms are excluded and no periodic images are used.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#fmm-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Implement leaf P2M, upward M2M, interaction-list M2L, downward L2L, local-polynomial evaluation and near-field P2P. Record translation and near-pair counts; this is not a Barnes–Hut traversal relabeled as FMM.
M_k(c)=\sum_jq_j(z_j-c)^kf(z)=M_0\log(z-c)-\sum_{k=1}^p\frac{M_k}{k(z-c)^k},\qquad\phi=-\Re f

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#fmm-validation
Coverage: reading

For 128 fixed-seed particles, sweep orders 2/4/8/12 and compare every potential/field component with a separate all-pairs calculation. Also check two-source signs, permutation invariance and potential derivatives.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#fmm-limits
Coverage: reading

No 3D 1/r kernel, adaptive tree, periodic FMM, singular quadrature or empirical complexity/scaling study. Evidence applies to this 2D free-space educational implementation.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Cold-plasma oscillation with electrostatic CIC PIC [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/
Coverage: reading

Couple electrons to a 1D periodic grid by CIC, solving Poisson and particle motion self-consistently.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#pic-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Dimensionless length 2pi, electron charge/mass −1, stationary ion density one and plasma frequency one. A quiet start receives a small sinusoidal displacement of amplitude 0.001.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#pic-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Combine CIC deposition and matching field gathering, a mean-zero spectral Poisson solve and velocity Verlet. Set the field Nyquist mode to zero for a real skew-adjoint spectral derivative.
\dot x_i=v_i,\quad\dot v_i=-E_h(x_i),\quad-\phi_{xx}=\rho,\quad E=-\phi_xA(t)/A(0)\simeq\cos(\omega_pt),\qquad\omega_p=1

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#pic-validation
Coverage: reading

Separate a 32/64/128-grid sweep from timestep refinement on a 512 grid. Compare displacement amplitude with continuum linear cos(t), and check charge compatibility, potential-Poisson residual and single-particle self force.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#pic-limits
Coverage: reading

Finite amplitude and finite particles leave an error floor. Nonlinear instabilities, Landau damping, collisions, electromagnetic/relativistic PIC and open particle boundaries are unvalidated.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Conservation and Maxwell relaxation in a homogeneous DSMC collision component [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/
Coverage: reading

Test conservation and relaxation toward equilibrium through randomized pair collisions of homogeneous Maxwell molecules.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#dsmc-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Homogeneous, equal masses, isotropic scattering and constant collision rate. Each round randomly matches every particle once. Two initial beams at ±sqrt(3) give target temperature one. Each seed has zero total momentum and fixed total energy: its finite-N equilibrium is microcanonical, while Maxwell/Gamma are large-N references.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#dsmc-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Preserve pair center-of-mass velocity and relative speed, then choose the new relative direction uniformly on the sphere. Rounds count collision operations and are not calibrated physical time. For D=<vx²−(vy²+vz²)/2>, averaging a random partner multiplies the center-of-mass anisotropy by (N−2)/(2(N−1)); isotropic postcollision relative directions contribute zero expected anisotropy.
\mathbf v_{1,2}^{\prime}=\mathbf V\pm\frac{|\mathbf g|}{2}\mathbf n,\qquad|\mathbf n|=1\mathbb E[D_{r+1}]=\frac{N-2}{2(N-1)}\mathbb E[D_r]

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#dsmc-validation
Coverage: reading

Use 512/2048/8192 particles and sixteen seeds to check momentum/energy, Maxwell second/fourth moments and the Gamma(3/2,1) energy CDF. Independently check the expected per-round anisotropy factor (N−2)/(2(N−1)). The finite-N component fourth moment is 3−6/(3N−1); distinguish that finite-particle offset from the across-seed sampling uncertainty.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#dsmc-limits
Coverage: reading

This is an educational DSMC collision component. No spatial streaming, collision cells, speed-dependent hard-sphere selection, measured transport coefficients/flow fields or every-seed guarantee. Bird’s original hard-sphere conditions are not reproduced.

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-kinetic-kernel-assumptions
Coverage: reading

kB=1, T=1.3, tau=0.5, h=0.2, 65536 independent replicas. Test three initial energies at each of three degree counts. No Hamiltonian force, positions, constraints or center-of-mass removal.

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-kinetic-kernel-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Use the completed-square exact CIR transition with normal R and independent chi-square(Nf−1) S. The same R sets the sign of global alpha; S=0 for Nf=1. Reconstruct momentum from its unit direction and new radius without a tiny-K energy ratio. Reject K=0 because its direction is undefined.
\bar K=\frac{N_fT}{2},\quad c=e^{-h/\tau},\quad A=\frac{T(1-c)}2,\quad R\sim N(0,1),\ S\sim\chi^2_{N_f-1}K^\prime=(\sqrt{cK}+\sqrt A R)^2+AS,\quad \operatorname{sign}\alpha=\operatorname{sign}(\sqrt{cK}+\sqrt A R)\mathbb E[K^\prime\mid K]=cK+(1-c)\bar K,\quad\operatorname{Var}(K^\prime\mid K)=2TKc(1-c)+\frac{N_fT^2}{2}(1-c)^2K\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(N_f/2,T),\quad\operatorname{Var}(T_{\rm inst})=\frac{2T^2}{N_f},\quad C_K^{\rm bath}(t)=e^{-t/\tau}

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-kinetic-kernel-validation
Coverage: reading

Compare with separate CIR conditional moments, three SciPy noncentral-chi-square quantile probabilities, stationary Gamma K and bath-only exp(−t/tau) correlation. A separate noiseless mean-relaxation control demonstrates loss of fluctuations.

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-kinetic-kernel-limits
Coverage: reading

A bath diagnostic, not another independent physical problem. Correct K sampling does not thermalize momentum directions by global scaling alone. The bath-only exp(−t/tau) identity is not a full-MD kinetic ACF. Statistical decisions apply to fixed seeds/budgets, not general mixing guarantees.

G. Bussi, D. Donadio and M. Parrinello (2007). Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling · DOI: 10.1063/1.2408420
Review scope / review_level: author-manuscript-selected-theory-and-appendix
Checked theory II.1–II.3 and the exact kinetic-energy propagator in Appendix A of the author manuscript arXiv:0803.4060v1 (posted 2008 for the 2007 article). The SISSA publisher PDF was unavailable. Original molecular applications are not reproduced. Direct chi-square sampling avoids copying the gamma-generation typo later noted by the author.
G. Bussi and M. Parrinello (2008). Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes · DOI: 10.1016/j.cpc.2008.01.006
Review scope / review_level: author-manuscript-selected-equations-and-algorithm
Checked sections I–II, finite-step update Eq. (8), the sign of alpha in Eq. (9) using the same Gaussian, the Nf=1 Langevin limit and tau=1/(2 gamma). The original long Lennard-Jones transport calculations are not reproduced.
Giovanni Bussi (2026). Research algorithms: stochastic velocity rescaling
Review scope / review_level: author-official-algorithm-note

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-langevin-harmonic-assumptions
Coverage: reading

m=kB=T=1, omega=(1,1.7), Nf=2. tau=0.25/1, h=0.1/0.05. Evolve 8192 canonically initialized replicas and a separate 4096-replica ensemble with q,p scaled by 1.4 to t=20. Correlation lags are 0/0.5/1/2/4.

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-langevin-harmonic-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Both use exact O(h/2)–velocity-Verlet–O(h/2), or OBABO. CSVR applies one factor to all momenta; Langevin uses independent component-wise OU noise. gamma=1/(2 tau) matches bath-only K relaxation. The earlier BAOAB release is retained as a different splitting.
U(q)=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^2\omega_i^2q_i^2,\quad H=K+U,\quad\gamma=\frac1{2\tau}\Sigma_{h,i}=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{T}{\omega_i^2(1-h^2\omega_i^2/4)},T\right),\quad\Sigma_h=M\Sigma_hM^T+QK\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(1,T),\quad H\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(2,T),\quad\operatorname{Var}K=T^2,\quad\operatorname{Var}H=2T^2C_X(t)=\frac{\mathbb E[(X_t-\mu_X)(X_0-\mu_X)]}{\sigma_X^2},\quad\operatorname{SE}(\widehat C_X)=\frac{s_{\rm products}}{\sqrt{N_{\rm replicas}}}

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-langevin-harmonic-validation
Coverage: reading

Check canonical Gaussian/Gamma distributions and K/U/H means/variances. For finite steps, compare the Verlet-shadow position variance T/[omega²(1−h² omega²/4)] and momentum variance T against a separately constructed Lyapunov solution. Deterministic biases at h=0.2/0.1/0.05 establish second order. Check Langevin q,p,K,H correlations against independent discrete propagation; report CSVR correlations with independent-replica standard errors and tau/h dependence.

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-langevin-harmonic-limits
Coverage: reading

Global-CSVR and local-Langevin dynamical correlations are not required to agree. CDF errors are maxima over five declared points, not whole-line KS distances. Canonical-start preservation and the heated-start finite-time check do not prove ergodicity; tests retain an invariant unexcited-axis counterexample. No extrapolation to molecules, constraints or BOMD.
